question: A team is deciding how to authenticate a mix of workloads: (1) a data scientist's laptop script for one-off prototyping, (2) a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every pull request, (3) a long-running Kubernetes deployment, and (4) a single-tenant on-prem server with no OIDC-capable identity provider available. For which of these should the team select an API key rather than Workload Identity Federation as the better fit? (Select all that apply.)
options: A) The GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every pull request.
B) The single-tenant on-prem server with no OIDC-capable identity provider available.
C) The data scientist's laptop script for one-off prototyping.
D) None of these; Workload Identity Federation is strictly better for every listed workload.
correct_answers: B) The single-tenant on-prem server with no OIDC-capable identity provider available.
C) The data scientist's laptop script for one-off prototyping.
explanations: Incorrect as a selection for API key preference. GitHub Actions is explicitly named as a supported WIF identity provider via its OIDC token, and CI/CD pipelines are called out as a best fit for WIF specifically to eliminate static secrets in CI.

Correct. Without an OIDC-capable identity provider, there is no federation issuer to register; an API key (with an appropriate expiration and secrets-manager storage) is the practical choice, matching the 'single-tenant servers' use case.
Correct. API keys are documented as best for local development, prototyping, scripts, and single-tenant servers where you control secret storage; a one-off laptop script fits this exactly.

Incorrect. The documentation explicitly recommends API keys over WIF for local development/prototyping and single-tenant servers where you control secret storage, so WIF is not strictly better across all four cases.

Incorrect as a selection for API key preference. Production workloads on cloud platforms including Kubernetes are the named best fit for WIF, since the platform already issues a workload identity that can be federated.
